1	# audit-chain
2	
3	Per-tenant audit log where every entry is chained to its predecessor, so a reader can verify a tenant history offline and pinpoint the first broken index.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit append <tenant> --payload <json-file>
16	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit verify <tenant>
17	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit recover
18	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit rotate
19	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit compact [--max-segments N]
20	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit export <tenant> --start N --end M > proof.json
21	    python3 -m audit_chain verify-proof proof.json [--tenant T] [--start N] [--end M]
22	
23	`--path` is either a single JSON-lines log file or a segment store
24	(directory); the first `rotate` migrates an existing file into a store at the
25	same path. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` verification found a broken entry
26	(including a tampered cache, manifest or sealed window), `2` any other error
27	(missing file, bad/half-written line, corrupt chain, bad payload type,
28	illegal proof range, lock contention, path/permission errors). Error paths
29	print nothing. `verify-proof` never opens the log.
30	
31	## Public interface
32	
33	`audit_chain.Chain(path)` opens the log file.
34	- `append(tenant, payload) -> dict` appends and returns the stored entry.
35	- `entries(tenant) -> list[dict]` returns entries in insertion order.
36	- `verify(tenant) -> dict` re-derives the chain and reports the first bad index.
37	- `head(tenant) -> str | None` returns the newest digest.
38	- `export_range(tenant, start, end) -> dict` builds an offline proof for the
39	  half-open interval `[start, end)` (see below).
40	
41	Additional entry points:
42	- `recover() -> {"truncated_bytes": n}` truncates a half-written tail line
43	  left by a killed process; complete but broken records are never repaired.
44	- `rotate()` seals the active segment and starts a new one.
45	- `compact(max_segments=2) -> {"segments": n}` merges old segments.
46	
47	`audit_chain.verify_proof(proof, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
48	verifies an exported proof with the public digest function alone; it never
49	touches the log.
50	
51	Two more offline entry points work purely on proof objects (no log):
52	- `audit_chain.combine_proofs(left, right) -> dict` splices two proofs of the
53	  same tenant whose intervals meet end-to-start (`left["end"] ==
54	  right["start"]`) into one ordinary proof covering the union
55	  `[left["start"], right["end"])`. It is associative, re-verifies both inputs
56	  and the result, and the combined proof checks out through `verify_proof`
57	  after the log itself has been compressed or deleted. A non-dict argument is
58	  `TypeError`; a side that is not a valid exporting proof or does not verify,
59	  or a tenant mismatch / gap / overlap / reversed order, is `ValueError`.
60	- `audit_chain.verify_proofs(proofs) -> list[dict]` verifies a batch and
61	  returns one verdict per proof, in input order, each with the same shape as
62	  the on-chain verdict. A tampered proof yields an `ok=False` verdict with the
63	  real global bad index without interrupting the rest. An empty list is
64	  `ValueError`; the argument or an element that is not a dict is `TypeError`.
65	
66	### Snapshot consistency
67	
68	`verify`, `entries` and `head` each run under a shared process lock and read
69	one fixed unit list in one ordered pass, while append/rotate/compact/recover
70	run under an exclusive lock. A single call therefore always observes one
71	complete prefix — the topology immediately before or immediately after a
72	rotation or merge — never mixed segments, a duplicated run or a skipped run.
73	
74	### Incremental, constant-read-amplification verification
75	
76	Concurrent appenders to one log are serialized by a cross-platform file lock
77	(`flock` on POSIX, `LockFileEx` on Windows), so records always link strictly
78	with continuous zero-based per-tenant indices. Each sealed segment keeps
79	byte-level verification material (size + sha256 per source segment, retained
80	through compaction). A repeat verify hashes only newly appended bytes plus a
81	small amount of sidecar material — never the whole file, and never a sealed
82	byte window on the hot path. The manifest is self-authenticating and the
83	verify cache is authenticated; tampering with the cache, the manifest or a
84	sealed window is reported as corruption (`ok=False`) with the real first bad
85	index rather than a pass. Tenants stay isolated: one tenant's damage never
86	changes another tenant's verdict.
87	
88	### Offline range proofs
89	
90	`export_range(tenant, start, end)` returns a self-contained proof for a
91	contiguous interval. It contains only the interval's chained records and the
92	strictly-increasing cross-segment window anchors (offset/size/sha256) needed
93	to attach them; no out-of-interval payload is included. An independent reader
94	recomputes every digest, checks predecessor links, indices, offsets and the
95	window chain using `verify_proof` (and the public digest) alone. Damage
96	outside the interval cannot affect its conclusion. Empty or reversed
97	intervals, non-integer or out-of-bounds ranges raise `ValueError`; a tenant
98	with no history returns a verifiable empty-history proof for `(0, 0)`.
99	
100	Two proofs exported from the same tenant can be joined with
101	`combine_proofs`: when their indices meet end-to-start the result is the same
102	kind of proof over the union, independently verifiable, and associating three
103	pieces pairwise gives the same conclusion as one proof over the whole range.
104	This holds with endpoints on segment boundaries, across segments merged by
105	compaction, and across the cross-segment window chain; it stays verifiable
106	after the log is compacted, corrupted or deleted. `verify_proofs` verifies
107	many proofs at once, one verdict each in order.
108	
109	### Export cost
110	
111	Exporting (and splicing, and batch verification) costs work proportional to
112	the interval, not to total history length. With a warm, authenticated verify
113	cache an export opens only the segment files that hold an interval record and
114	reads no others; records in sealed segments are anchored straight from the
115	signed manifest material, so sealed bytes are never hashed, and records in the
116	still-growing tail are anchored over small windows containing only the
117	interval's own lines. A never-verified or altered store transparently falls
118	back to a full ordered byte scan with identical conclusions.
119	
120	### Crash recovery
121	
122	Every commit is a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename, and a merge
123	publishes its bytes before swapping the manifest and only removes old
124	segments afterwards. A process hard-killed in any window (partial write,
125	flush/fsync, segment rename, manifest replacement, old-segment deletion)
126	reopens onto either the old topology or the complete new one: a migration
127	backup is adopted, a staged directory / orphan segment / residual temp file
128	is reaped by the next writer, and a half-written tail line keeps its bad-line
129	semantics until `recover()` truncates it.
130	
131	## Tests
132	
133	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
134	
135	The suite includes a real-kill crash-injection matrix (separate processes
136	hard-killed at each commit window), concurrent snapshot-consistency stress,
137	tamper-evidence tests and offline-proof tests.
138	
139	## Limits
140	
141	Payloads must be JSON-serialisable.
142	No network service and no remote anchoring.

# audit-chain

Per-tenant audit log where every entry is chained to its predecessor, so a reader can verify a tenant history offline and pinpoint the first broken index.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit append <tenant> --payload <json-file>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit verify <tenant>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit recover
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit rotate
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit compact [--max-segments N]
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit export <tenant> --start N --end M > proof.json
    python3 -m audit_chain verify-proof proof.json [--tenant T] [--start N] [--end M]

`--path` is either a single JSON-lines log file or a segment store
(directory); the first `rotate` migrates an existing file into a store at the
same path. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` verification found a broken entry
(including a tampered cache, manifest or sealed window), `2` any other error
(missing file, bad/half-written line, corrupt chain, bad payload type,
illegal proof range, lock contention, path/permission errors). Error paths
print nothing. `verify-proof` never opens the log.

## Public interface

`audit_chain.Chain(path)` opens the log file.
- `append(tenant, payload) -> dict` appends and returns the stored entry.
- `entries(tenant) -> list[dict]` returns entries in insertion order.
- `verify(tenant) -> dict` re-derives the chain and reports the first bad index.
- `head(tenant) -> str | None` returns the newest digest.
- `export_range(tenant, start, end) -> dict` builds an offline proof for the
  half-open interval `[start, end)` (see below).

Additional entry points:
- `recover() -> {"truncated_bytes": n}` truncates a half-written tail line
  left by a killed process; complete but broken records are never repaired.
- `rotate()` seals the active segment and starts a new one.
- `compact(max_segments=2) -> {"segments": n}` merges old segments.

`audit_chain.verify_proof(proof, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
verifies an exported proof with the public digest function alone; it never
touches the log.

Two more offline entry points work purely on proof objects (no log):
- `audit_chain.combine_proofs(left, right) -> dict` splices two proofs of the
  same tenant whose intervals meet end-to-start (`left["end"] ==
  right["start"]`) into one ordinary proof covering the union
  `[left["start"], right["end"])`. It is associative, re-verifies both inputs
  and the result, and the combined proof checks out through `verify_proof`
  after the log itself has been compressed or deleted. A non-dict argument is
  `TypeError`; a side that is not a valid exporting proof or does not verify,
  or a tenant mismatch / gap / overlap / reversed order, is `ValueError`.
- `audit_chain.verify_proofs(proofs) -> list[dict]` verifies a batch and
  returns one verdict per proof, in input order, each with the same shape as
  the on-chain verdict. A tampered proof yields an `ok=False` verdict with the
  real global bad index without interrupting the rest. An empty list is
  `ValueError`; the argument or an element that is not a dict is `TypeError`.

### Snapshot consistency

`verify`, `entries` and `head` each run under a shared process lock and read
one fixed unit list in one ordered pass, while append/rotate/compact/recover
run under an exclusive lock. A single call therefore always observes one
complete prefix — the topology immediately before or immediately after a
rotation or merge — never mixed segments, a duplicated run or a skipped run.

### Incremental, constant-read-amplification verification

Concurrent appenders to one log are serialized by a cross-platform file lock
(`flock` on POSIX, `LockFileEx` on Windows), so records always link strictly
with continuous zero-based per-tenant indices. Each sealed segment keeps
byte-level verification material (size + sha256 per source segment, retained
through compaction). A repeat verify hashes only newly appended bytes plus a
small amount of sidecar material — never the whole file, and never a sealed
byte window on the hot path. The manifest is self-authenticating and the
verify cache is authenticated; tampering with the cache, the manifest or a
sealed window is reported as corruption (`ok=False`) with the real first bad
index rather than a pass. Tenants stay isolated: one tenant's damage never
changes another tenant's verdict.

### Offline range proofs

`export_range(tenant, start, end)` returns a self-contained proof for a
contiguous interval. It contains only the interval's chained records and the
strictly-increasing cross-segment window anchors (offset/size/sha256) needed
to attach them; no out-of-interval payload is included. An independent reader
recomputes every digest, checks predecessor links, indices, offsets and the
window chain using `verify_proof` (and the public digest) alone. Damage
outside the interval cannot affect its conclusion. Empty or reversed
intervals, non-integer or out-of-bounds ranges raise `ValueError`; a tenant
with no history returns a verifiable empty-history proof for `(0, 0)`.

Two proofs exported from the same tenant can be joined with
`combine_proofs`: when their indices meet end-to-start the result is the same
kind of proof over the union, independently verifiable, and associating three
pieces pairwise gives the same conclusion as one proof over the whole range.
This holds with endpoints on segment boundaries, across segments merged by
compaction, and across the cross-segment window chain; it stays verifiable
after the log is compacted, corrupted or deleted. `verify_proofs` verifies
many proofs at once, one verdict each in order.

### Export cost

Exporting (and splicing, and batch verification) costs work proportional to
the interval, not to total history length. With a warm, authenticated verify
cache an export opens only the segment files that hold an interval record and
reads no others; records in sealed segments are anchored straight from the
signed manifest material, so sealed bytes are never hashed, and records in the
still-growing tail are anchored over small windows containing only the
interval's own lines. A never-verified or altered store transparently falls
back to a full ordered byte scan with identical conclusions.

### Crash recovery

Every commit is a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename, and a merge
publishes its bytes before swapping the manifest and only removes old
segments afterwards. A process hard-killed in any window (partial write,
flush/fsync, segment rename, manifest replacement, old-segment deletion)
reopens onto either the old topology or the complete new one: a migration
backup is adopted, a staged directory / orphan segment / residual temp file
is reaped by the next writer, and a half-written tail line keeps its bad-line
semantics until `recover()` truncates it.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

The suite includes a real-kill crash-injection matrix (separate processes
hard-killed at each commit window), concurrent snapshot-consistency stress,
tamper-evidence tests and offline-proof tests.

## Limits

Payloads must be JSON-serialisable.
No network service and no remote anchoring.

9	
10	* concurrent appenders to the same log are serialized by a process-shared,
11	  cross-platform file lock, so interlocked writes still link strictly;
12	* every read (``verify``/``entries``/``head``) takes a snapshot under a
13	  shared lock: a single call always sees one complete prefix -- the old
14	  topology or the new one around a rotation, merge or recovery -- never a
15	  mix of segments, a duplicate run or a skipped run;
16	* the log can be rotated into ordered segment files and compacted, with
17	  every source segment's verification material (byte size + sha256)
18	  retained through merges, committed by an atomic, self-authenticating
19	  manifest replacement; merged bytes are published through a temp file and
20	  rename, so every crash window lands on the old or the new topology;
21	* verification of long logs is incremental: unchanged byte windows are
22	  authenticated by an on-disk cache (stat-guarded on the active unit,
23	  window-material-guarded on sealed units), so a repeated verification of
24	  a ten-thousand-entry log only hashes newly appended bytes plus a small
25	  amount of sidecar material;
26	* tampering with the cache, the manifest or a sealed window is reported as
27	  chain corruption with the real first bad global index (never a pass, and
28	  distinct from the half-line bad-line semantics);
29	* ``export_range`` produces an offline proof for a contiguous index
30	  interval: only the interval's records plus the window anchors needed to
31	  attach the chain, verifiable with the public digest alone;
32	* ``recover`` is the explicit entry point that truncates a half-written
33	  tail line left by a killed process.
34	"""

52	class Chain:
53	    """Append-only, per-tenant hash-chained audit log."""
54	
55	    def __init__(
56	        self,
57	        path: str,
58	        *,
59	        lock_timeout: Optional[float] = _DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT,
60	    ):
61	        self.path = path
62	        self.lock_timeout = lock_timeout
63	
64	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
65	    # Layout / locking
66	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
67	
68	    def _lock_path(self) -> str:
69	        normalized = os.path.normpath(self.path)
70	        parent = os.path.dirname(normalized) or "."
71	        return os.path.join(parent, "." + os.path.basename(normalized) + ".lock")
72	
73	    def _layout(self) -> st.Layout:
74	        existing = st.resolve_existing(self.path)
75	        if existing is not None:
76	            return existing
77	        # Nothing on disk yet: stay in the legacy file layout until the
78	        # first append (or an explicit rotate) creates anything.
79	        return st.Layout(self.path, "file")
80	
81	    def _needs_adoption(self) -> bool:
82	        backup = self.path + ".pre-segment"
83	        return not os.path.exists(self.path) and os.path.exists(backup)
84	
85	    @contextlib.contextmanager
86	    def _locked(self, *, exclusive: bool):
87	        # Readers open shared. A tree left mid-operation by a killed process
88	        # is not in a quiescent state (backup to adopt, staging dir, merge
89	        # temp file or an unreferenced segment); such a reader escalates
90	        # once to an exclusive lock, heals the tree deterministically, and
91	        # only then reads. In a quiescent tree no escalation happens, so the
92	        # ordinary read path stays shared.
93	        want_exclusive = exclusive or self._needs_adoption()
94	        while True:
95	            with st.file_lock(
96	                self._lock_path(), timeout=self.lock_timeout, shared=not want_exclusive
97	            ):
98	                if not want_exclusive:
99	                    layout = st.resolve_existing(self.path)
100	                    if layout is None:
101	                        layout = st.Layout(self.path, "file")
102	                    if self._needs_healing(layout):
103	                        want_exclusive = True
104	                        continue  # release the shared lock, re-enter exclusive
105	                    yield layout
106	                    return
107	
108	                self._adopt_backup()
109	                layout = st.resolve_existing(self.path)
110	                if layout is None:
111	                    layout = st.Layout(self.path, "file")
112	                self._reap_crash_leftovers(layout)
113	                yield layout
114	                return
115	
116	    def _needs_healing(self, layout: st.Layout) -> bool:
117	        """Whether a shared read must escalate to heal before reading.
118	
119	        A read only escalates when the live path is absent and a migration
120	        backup is waiting -- without adoption there is nothing to read.
121	        Every other leftover (staging directory, an unreferenced segment
122	        from a rotation/compaction killed before/after its manifest commit,
123	        a merge temp file, a post-publish backup) is inert while the
124	        committed manifest stays authoritative, so reads leave it untouched
125	        and the next writer (exclusive) reaps it -- matching the baseline
126	        rule that reads never move garbage out from under other readers.
127	        """
128	        return not os.path.exists(self.path) and os.path.exists(
129	            self.path + ".pre-segment"
130	        )
131	
132	    def _reap_crash_leftovers(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
133	        """Deterministically finish every crash window's housekeeping."""
134	        backup = self.path + ".pre-segment"
135	        staging = self.path + ".segstage"
136	        if layout.kind == "file":
137	            # The store never happened: drop any staged directory and let
138	            # _adopt_backup move the file back.
139	            if os.path.isdir(staging):
140	                self._remove_tree(staging)
141	            return
142	
143	        # The segment store is the published topology. A backup left behind
144	        # means the migration was killed right after publishing the store.
145	        if os.path.exists(backup):
146	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
147	                os.remove(backup)
148	                st.fsync_dir(os.path.dirname(self.path) or ".")
149	        if os.path.isdir(staging):
150	            self._remove_tree(staging)
151	
152	        manifest = None
153	        with contextlib.suppress(st.AuditMetadataError):
154	            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
155	        if manifest is not None:
156	            self._gc_segments(layout, manifest)
157	        # Temp files of killed atomic writes/merges (never the lock).
158	        if os.path.isdir(layout.root):
159	            for name in os.listdir(layout.root):
160	                if name.startswith(".") and name.endswith(".tmp"):
161	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
162	                        os.remove(os.path.join(layout.root, name))
163	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
164	
165	    @staticmethod
166	    def _remove_tree(path: str) -> None:
167	        import shutil
168	
169	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
170	            shutil.rmtree(path)
171	
172	    def _adopt_backup(self) -> None:
173	        """Restore a log left behind by a migration killed mid-rename.
174	
175	        rotate() renames the legacy file aside before putting the segment
176	        store in its place; if the process is killed between the two renames,
177	        the file survives as a backup and is moved back on the next open.
178	        """
179	        backup = self.path + ".pre-segment"
180	        staging = self.path + ".segstage"
181	        if os.path.exists(self.path) or not os.path.exists(backup):
182	            return
183	        if os.path.isdir(staging):
184	            self._remove_tree(staging)
185	        parent = os.path.dirname(self.path) or "."
186	        os.replace(backup, self.path)
187	        st.fsync_dir(parent)

189	    def _view(self, layout: st.Layout) -> list[dict]:
190	        """Ordered units that make up the log, oldest first.
191	
192	        A unit is the legacy single file or one manifest segment. Sealed
193	        units carry preserved byte windows (verification material); the
194	        active unit and the legacy file are fingerprinted as they grow.
195	        """
196	        if layout.kind == "file":
197	            return [
198	                {
199	                    "name": _FILE_UNIT,
200	                    "path": layout.root,
201	                    "sealed": False,
202	                    "parts": [],
203	                }
204	            ]
205	
206	        manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
207	        if manifest is None:
208	            # Segment stores are created atomically (manifest + first
209	            # segment) by rotate(); a directory without one is a path
210	            # collision, never an implicit store.
211	            raise ValueError("missing audit manifest")
212	
213	        return [
214	            {
215	                "name": segment["name"],
216	                "path": layout.segment_path(segment["name"]),
217	                "sealed": segment["sealed"],
218	                "parts": [dict(part) for part in segment["parts"]],
219	            }
220	            for segment in manifest["segments"]
221	        ]
222	
223	    def _raw_units(self, layout: st.Layout) -> list[dict]:
224	        """Units reconstructed from ordered segment file names alone.
225	
226	        Used when the manifest cannot be trusted: the records themselves
227	        still carry the chain, so the real first bad index stays derivable.
228	        """
229	        if layout.kind == "file":
230	            return self._view(layout)
231	        names = sorted(
232	            name
233	            for name in os.listdir(layout.root)
234	            if st.seg_seq(name) is not None
235	        )
236	        return [
237	            {
238	                "name": name,
239	                "path": layout.segment_path(name),
240	                "sealed": False,
241	                "parts": [],
242	            }
243	            for name in names
244	        ]

246	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
247	    # Raw reads (entries/head; structure only, no chain or cache)
248	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
249	
250	    def _all_records(self, units: list[dict], *, missing_empty: bool) -> list[dict]:
251	        records: list[dict] = []
252	        for unit in units:
253	            try:
254	                raw = st.scan_segment_bytes(unit["path"])
255	            except FileNotFoundError:
256	                if missing_empty and not unit["sealed"]:
257	                    continue
258	                raise
259	            records.extend(st.decode_records(raw))
260	        return records
261	
262	    def _snapshot_units(
263	        self, layout: st.Layout, *, tolerate_metadata: bool
264	    ) -> list[dict]:
265	        try:
266	            return self._view(layout)
267	        except st.AuditMetadataError:
268	            if not tolerate_metadata:
269	                raise
270	            return self._raw_units(layout)
271	
272	    def _tenant_records(self, tenant: str, *, missing_empty: bool) -> list[dict]:
273	        with self._locked(exclusive=False) as layout:
274	            if layout.kind == "file" and not os.path.exists(layout.root):
275	                if missing_empty:
276	                    return []
277	                raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
278	            # One fixed unit list and one ordered byte read under the shared
279	            # lock: writers (exclusive) cannot rotate, merge or recover
280	            # mid-call, so the result is always one complete prefix.
281	            units = self._snapshot_units(layout, tolerate_metadata=True)
282	            records = self._all_records(units, missing_empty=missing_empty)
283	        return [record for record in records if record["tenant"] == tenant]
284	
285	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
286	    # Public read API (unchanged shapes)
287	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
288	
289	    def entries(self, tenant: str) -> list[dict]:
290	        """Return all of the tenant's records in insertion order."""
291	        return self._tenant_records(tenant, missing_empty=True)
292	
293	    def head(self, tenant: str) -> Optional[str]:
294	        """Return the tenant's newest digest, or None for an empty chain."""
295	        records = self._tenant_records(tenant, missing_empty=True)
296	        if not records:
297	            return None
298	        return records[-1]["digest"]

300	    def verify(self, tenant: str) -> dict:
301	        """Re-derive the tenant's chain, incrementally across segments.
302	
303	        Returns ``{"count": n, "first_bad": i, "ok": bool}`` with global,
304	        zero-based per-tenant indices. Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` when the
305	        log is absent and ``ValueError`` on a bad or half-written line.
306	        Tampering with the cache, the manifest or a sealed window is itself
307	        corruption: the verdict is ``ok=False`` with the real first bad
308	        index rather than an exception.
309	        """
310	        metadata_damaged = False
311	        with self._locked(exclusive=False) as layout:
312	            self._require_present(layout)
313	            try:
314	                units = self._view(layout)
315	            except st.AuditMetadataError:
316	                # A rewritten manifest cannot vouch for any window: fall
317	                # back to the physically ordered segment files and re-derive
318	                # every link from the bytes themselves.
319	                metadata_damaged = True
320	                units = self._raw_units(layout)
321	
322	            try:
323	                states, _ = self._walk(
324	                    units,
325	                    layout,
326	                    ignore_cache=metadata_damaged,
327	                    persist=not metadata_damaged,
328	                )
329	            except st.AuditMetadataError:
330	                # The sidecar cache was tampered with. It is neither trusted
331	                # nor silently healed: re-derive from bytes and report the
332	                # metadata damage as corruption below.
333	                metadata_damaged = True
334	                states, _ = self._walk(units, layout, ignore_cache=True, persist=False)
335	
336	        state = states.get(tenant)
337	        if state is None:
338	            return {"count": 0, "first_bad": -1, "ok": True}
339	        count, _head, bad = state
340	        if bad != -1:
341	            # The byte-level walk found the real break first; it always
342	            # outranks the metadata tripwire.
343	            return {"count": count, "first_bad": bad, "ok": False}
344	        if metadata_damaged:
345	            # The bytes still re-derive, but authentication material the
346	            # chain depended on (manifest windows or the verified cache) was
347	            # rewritten: the earliest index it could vouch for is 0.
348	            return {"count": count, "first_bad": 0, "ok": False}
349	        return {"count": count, "first_bad": -1, "ok": True}
350	
351	    def _require_present(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
352	        if layout.kind == "file":
353	            if not os.path.isfile(layout.root):
354	                raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
355	            return
356	        # An existing directory without a manifest is malformed; let the
357	        # view report it rather than masking it as a missing file.
358	        if not os.path.isdir(layout.root):
359	            raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
360	
361	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
362	    # Append
363	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
364	
365	    def append(self, tenant: str, payload: Any) -> dict:
366	        """Append one record for ``tenant`` and return the stored entry.
367	
368	        Raises ``TypeError`` for a non-object payload and ``ValueError`` if
369	        the existing log, its cache or its manifest is corrupt; existing
370	        records are left untouched. Concurrent appenders are serialized by
371	        a file lock.
372	        """
373	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
374	            raise TypeError("payload must be a dict")
375	
376	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
377	            units = self._view(layout)
378	
379	            # Refuse to extend a damaged log.
380	            states, _ = self._walk(units, layout)
381	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
382	                if bad != -1:
383	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
384	
385	            prev = states.get(tenant, (0, "", -1))[1]
386	            record, line = rec.build_line(tenant, payload, prev)
387	            target = units[-1]["path"]
388	            data = (line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING)
389	            # Two raw writes with a real kill point between them model the
390	            # write/flush/fsync crash window: a kill after the first syscall
391	            # leaves a deterministic half line that reopen treats as a bad
392	            # line, never as a silently repaired record.
393	            cut = max(1, len(data) // 2)
394	            fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o600)
395	            try:
396	                _write_all(fd, data[:cut])
397	                st.crash_point("append:after_first_write")
398	                _write_all(fd, data[cut:])
399	                st.crash_point("append:before_fsync")
400	                os.fsync(fd)
401	                st.crash_point("append:after_fsync")
402	            finally:
403	                os.close(fd)
404	
405	            # Warm the cache with the single record just written: suffix
406	            # only, never a rehash of the whole file. This call is still
407	            # inside the exclusive lock and the prefix could not have changed
408	            # since the states above were computed, so the continuation is
409	            # trusted by construction.
410	            self._walk(self._view(layout), layout, trust_growth=True)
411	        return record
412	
413	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
414	    # Crash recovery
415	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
416	
417	    def recover(self) -> dict:
418	        """Truncate a half-written tail line left by a crashed append.
419	
420	        Only the physical trailing partial line of the active log is
421	        removed; complete but chain-broken records are never silently
422	        repaired. Returns the number of bytes removed. The verify cache is
423	        discarded because the bytes legitimately shrank.
424	        """
425	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
426	            self._require_present(layout)
427	            units = self._view(layout)
428	            target = units[-1]["path"]
429	
430	            with open(target, "rb") as handle:
431	                raw = handle.read()
432	            if raw == b"" or raw.endswith(b"\n"):
433	                return {"truncated_bytes": 0}
434	
435	            cut = raw.rfind(b"\n") + 1
436	            removed = len(raw) - cut
437	            # Drop the cache before changing bytes: whichever window a kill
438	            # lands in, reopen never mistakes the legitimate shrink for a
439	            # cached deletion (either the half line still reads as a bad
440	            # line, or the cache is already gone and the prefix re-derives).
441	            self._delete_cache(layout)
442	            fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY)
443	            try:
444	                os.ftruncate(fd, cut)
445	                st.crash_point("recover:after_truncate")
446	                os.fsync(fd)
447	            finally:
448	                os.close(fd)
449	        return {"truncated_bytes": removed}

451	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
452	    # Rotation and compaction
453	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
454	
455	    def rotate(self) -> None:
456	        """Cut a new active segment.
457	
458	        On a legacy single-file log this first migrates the file into a
459	        segment store at the same path, sealing the original bytes as the
460	        first segment. On an already segmented log the active segment is
461	        sealed (its preserved windows plus one window for the bytes appended
462	        after them) and a fresh empty segment becomes active.
463	        """
464	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
465	            if layout.kind == "file":
466	                self._migrate_file(layout)
467	            else:
468	                self._rotate_dir(layout)
469	
470	    def _migrate_file(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
471	        path = layout.root
472	        raw = b""
473	        if os.path.exists(path):
474	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
475	                raw = handle.read()
476	            # A crashed half-line must be recovered, not silently migrated.
477	            st.decode_records(raw)
478	
479	        parent = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
480	        staging = path + ".segstage"
481	        backup = path + ".pre-segment"
482	        if os.path.exists(backup):
483	            os.remove(backup)
484	        os.mkdir(staging)
485	        try:
486	            if raw:
487	                first = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ)
488	                second = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ + 1)
489	                self._write_bytes(staging, first, raw)
490	                self._write_bytes(staging, second, b"")
491	                manifest = {
492	                    "version": 1,
493	                    "active": second,
494	                    "segments": [
495	                        {
496	                            "name": first,
497	                            "sealed": True,
498	                            "parts": [
499	                                {
500	                                    "name": first,
501	                                    "size": len(raw),
502	                                    "sha256": _sha256(raw),
503	                                }
504	                            ],
505	                        },
506	                        {"name": second, "sealed": False, "parts": []},
507	                    ],
508	                }
509	            else:
510	                first = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ)
511	                self._write_bytes(staging, first, b"")
512	                manifest = st.default_manifest(first)
513	            st.save_manifest_at(staging, manifest)
514	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_staging")
515	
516	            # Keep the old data until the new store is in place: rename it
517	            # aside, publish the store, then drop the backup. Every kill in
518	            # between lands on one topology and is healed on next open.
519	            committed = False
520	            if os.path.exists(path):
521	                os.replace(path, backup)
522	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
523	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_backup_rename")
524	            try:
525	                os.replace(staging, path)
526	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
527	                committed = True
528	            finally:
529	                if not committed:
530	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
531	                        os.replace(backup, path)
532	                        st.fsync_dir(parent)
533	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_publish")
534	            if os.path.exists(backup):
535	                os.remove(backup)
536	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
537	        except BaseException:
538	            # Roll the staging directory back out; the original file lives on
539	            # as the backup until the new store is fully published.
540	            if os.path.isdir(staging):
541	                for name in os.listdir(staging):
542	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
543	                        os.unlink(os.path.join(staging, name))
544	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
545	                    os.rmdir(staging)
546	            raise
547	
548	        # The lock is topology-independent and stays put; the legacy sidecar
549	        # described the former single file, whereas the store's cache lives
550	        # inside the directory. Drop the stale one and warm the store's cache
551	        # from the bytes just migrated (mirrors _rotate_dir), so an export
552	        # right after the first rotation need not cold-scan the history.
553	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
554	            os.remove(layout.cache_path)
555	        new_layout = st.Layout(self.path, "dir")
556	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError, ValueError):
557	            self._walk(self._view(new_layout), new_layout)
558	
559	    def _rotate_dir(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
560	        units = self._view(layout)
561	        manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
562	        active_name = manifest["active"]
563	        active_unit = next(unit for unit in units if unit["name"] == active_name)
564	        active_manifest = next(
565	            segment for segment in manifest["segments"] if segment["name"] == active_name
566	        )
567	        size = os.path.getsize(active_unit["path"])
568	        if size == 0:
569	            return
570	
571	        # Walk first so a corrupt active segment cannot be sealed away.
572	        states, entries = self._walk(units, layout)
573	        for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
574	            if bad != -1:
575	                raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
576	
577	        # Freeze the active bytes as verification material: keep windows the
578	        # segment already preserved (e.g. from a fold-to-one compaction) and
579	        # add one window for the bytes appended after them.
580	        with open(active_unit["path"], "rb") as handle:
581	            active_bytes = handle.read()
582	        sealed_prefix = sum(part["size"] for part in active_manifest["parts"])
583	        seal_parts = [dict(part) for part in active_manifest["parts"]]
584	        if seal_parts and not st.verify_prefix_windows(
585	            active_unit["path"], seal_parts
586	        ):
587	            raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
588	        if len(active_bytes) > sealed_prefix:
589	            seal_parts.append(
590	                {
591	                    "name": active_name,
592	                    "size": len(active_bytes) - sealed_prefix,
593	                    "sha256": _sha256(active_bytes[sealed_prefix:]),
594	                }
595	            )
596	        entries[active_name]["parts"] = [dict(part) for part in seal_parts]
597	        for segment in manifest["segments"]:
598	            if segment["name"] == active_name:
599	                segment["sealed"] = True
600	                segment["parts"] = seal_parts
601	        next_seq = max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in manifest["segments"]) + 1
602	        new_active = st.seg_name(next_seq)
603	        # The new segment is an unreferenced orphan until the manifest commit
604	        # names it; a kill in this window simply has it garbage-collected and
605	        # the old topology remains authoritative.
606	        self._write_bytes(layout.root, new_active, b"")
607	        st.crash_point("rotate:before_manifest")
608	        manifest["segments"].append(
609	            {"name": new_active, "sealed": False, "parts": []}
610	        )
611	        manifest["active"] = new_active
612	        st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
613	        st.crash_point("rotate:after_manifest")
614	        st.save_cache(layout, entries)

616	    def compact(self, max_segments: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_SEGMENTS) -> dict:
617	        """Merge old sealed segments while keeping each one's material.
618	
619	        The log is folded until at most ``max_segments`` segments remain
620	        (the active segment counts). Each merge concatenates the source
621	        bytes and retains their ordered (size, sha256) windows, so every
622	        source segment's verification material survives compression and the
623	        global insertion order is unchanged.
624	
625	        Merged bytes are staged in a temp file and renamed before the
626	        atomic manifest commit; the old segments are removed only after the
627	        commit. A kill at any point therefore leaves the old topology or
628	        the complete new topology plus unreferenced files reaped on reopen.
629	        """
630	        if max_segments < 1:
631	            raise ValueError("max_segments must be >= 1")
632	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
633	            if layout.kind != "dir":
634	                raise ValueError("log is not segmented; call rotate() first")
635	            units = self._view(layout)
636	
637	            # Never fold a damaged log.
638	            states, _ = self._walk(units, layout)
639	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
640	                if bad != -1:
641	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
642	
643	            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
644	            cache = st.load_cache(layout)
645	            cache_segments = {} if cache is None else dict(cache["segments"])
646	
647	            if max_segments == 1 and len(manifest["segments"]) > 1:
648	                removed = self._merge_all(layout, manifest, cache_segments)
649	            else:
650	                removed: list[str] = []
651	                while len(manifest["segments"]) > max_segments:
652	                    removed += self._merge_pair(layout, manifest, cache_segments)
653	
654	            if removed:
655	                # Commit the new topology first; the now-unreferenced
656	                # sources are removed after the durable manifest swap and
657	                # otherwise garbage collected on the next open, so a crash
658	                # never loses data and never exposes a mixed topology.
659	                st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
660	                st.crash_point("compact:after_manifest")
661	                st.save_cache(layout, cache_segments)
662	                for name in removed:
663	                    with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
664	                        os.remove(layout.segment_path(name))
665	                    st.crash_point("compact:during_delete")
666	                st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
667	                st.crash_point("compact:after_delete")
668	            count = len(manifest["segments"])
669	        return {"segments": count}

671	    def _gc_segments(self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
672	        """Remove segment files not referenced by the committed manifest."""
673	        referenced = {segment["name"] for segment in manifest["segments"]}
674	        changed = False
675	        for name in os.listdir(layout.root):
676	            if st.seg_seq(name) is not None and name not in referenced:
677	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
678	                    os.remove(layout.segment_path(name))
679	                    changed = True
680	        if changed:
681	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)

683	    def _publish_bytes(self, layout: st.Layout, name: str, raw: bytes) -> str:
684	        """Stage ``raw`` in a temp file and rename it to segment ``name``."""
685	        target = layout.segment_path(name)
686	        tmp_path = os.path.join(layout.root, st._tmp_name_for(name))
687	        try:
688	            fd = os.open(tmp_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
689	            try:
690	                _write_all(fd, raw)
691	                st.crash_point("compact:before_merge_fsync")
692	                os.fsync(fd)
693	            finally:
694	                os.close(fd)
695	            st.crash_point("compact:after_merge_write")
696	            os.replace(tmp_path, target)
697	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
698	            st.crash_point("compact:after_merge_rename")
699	        except BaseException:
700	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
701	                os.remove(tmp_path)
702	            raise
703	        return target

705	    def _merge_all(
706	        self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict, cache_segments: dict
707	    ) -> list[str]:
708	        """Fold every segment, active included, into one active segment."""
709	        sources = manifest["segments"]
710	        merged, parts, carried = self._compose(layout, sources, cache_segments)
711	        name = st.seg_name(max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in sources) + 1)
712	        target = self._publish_bytes(layout, name, merged)
713	        for source in sources:
714	            cache_segments.pop(source["name"], None)
715	        if carried is not None:
716	            cache_segments[name] = _cache_entry(
717	                carried["records"],
718	                os.stat(target),
719	                parts,
720	                _states_from(carried),
721	                _fold_of_bytes(merged),
722	            )
723	        manifest["segments"] = [
724	            {"name": name, "sealed": False, "parts": parts}
725	        ]
726	        manifest["active"] = name
727	        return [source["name"] for source in sources]

729	    def _merge_pair(
730	        self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict, cache_segments: dict
731	    ) -> list[str]:
732	        """Merge the two oldest segments into one new sealed segment."""
733	        sources = manifest["segments"][:2]
734	        merged, parts, carried = self._compose(layout, sources, cache_segments)
735	        name = st.seg_name(
736	            max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in manifest["segments"]) + 1
737	        )
738	        target = self._publish_bytes(layout, name, merged)
739	        manifest["segments"] = [
740	            {"name": name, "sealed": True, "parts": parts}
741	        ] + manifest["segments"][2:]
742	        for source in sources:
743	            cache_segments.pop(source["name"], None)
744	        if carried is not None:
745	            cache_segments[name] = _cache_entry(
746	                carried["records"],
747	                os.stat(target),
748	                parts,
749	                _states_from(carried),
750	                _fold_of_bytes(merged),
751	            )
752	        return [source["name"] for source in sources]

754	    def _compose(
755	        self, layout: st.Layout, sources: list[dict], cache_segments: dict
756	    ) -> tuple[bytes, list[dict], Optional[dict]]:
757	        """Concatenate source bytes and windows, carrying warm cached states."""
758	        chunks: list[bytes] = []
759	        parts: list[dict] = []
760	        for source in sources:
761	            path = layout.segment_path(source["name"])
762	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
763	                data = handle.read()
764	            if source["sealed"]:
765	                windows = source["parts"]
766	                if len(data) != sum(w["size"] for w in windows) or not st.verify_windows(
767	                    path, windows
768	                ):
769	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
770	            else:
771	                # The active segment carries no preserved byte windows;
772	                # freeze one full-content window for it now (read once).
773	                windows = [
774	                    {
775	                        "name": source["name"],
776	                        "size": len(data),
777	                        "sha256": _sha256(data),
778	                    }
779	                ]
780	            chunks.append(data)
781	            parts.extend(dict(part) for part in windows)
782	
783	        # Cache entries hold cumulative per-tenant states, so after the
784	        # sources in order the last cached entry describes the whole merge.
785	        carried: Optional[dict] = None
786	        for source in sources:
787	            cached = cache_segments.get(source["name"])
788	            if cached is None:
789	                carried = None
790	                break
791	            carried = {
792	                "records": cached["records"],
793	                "tenants": {
794	                    tenant: list(state) for tenant, state in cached["tenants"].items()
795	                },
796	            }
797	        return b"".join(chunks), parts, carried

804	    def _walk(
805	        self,
806	        units: list[dict],
807	        layout: st.Layout,
808	        *,
809	        ignore_cache: bool = False,
810	        persist: bool = True,
811	        trust_growth: bool = False,
812	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]], dict]:
813	        """Walk every unit in order, reusing authenticated cached prefixes.
814	
815	        Returns ``(states, entries)``: states maps tenant to
816	        ``(count, head_digest, first_bad)``; entries maps unit name to its
817	        cache entry. Cost model:
818	
819	        * a unit unchanged since caching adopts the cached states with no
820	          record reads or digest work -- the active unit is stat-guarded and
821	          a sealed unit is guarded by its preserved window material, so no
822	          sealed byte is hashed on the hot path;
823	        * a grown active/legacy unit parses and chains only the appended
824	          suffix, so a ten-thousand-entry re-verify never rehashes the file;
825	        * a sealed segment is authenticated by its preserved byte windows
826	          (merged segments keep one window per source segment), and damaged
827	          windows are attributed to the tenants whose records they hold, so
828	          one tenant's corruption never changes another tenant's verdict
829	          while ``first_bad`` stays the global per-tenant index.
830	        """
831	        cache = None if ignore_cache else st.load_cache(layout)
832	        cached = {} if cache is None else cache["segments"]
833	        states: dict[str, list] = {}
834	        entries: dict[str, dict] = {}
835	        total_records = 0
836	        # Once any unit is re-walked outside its cache, the cached cumulative
837	        # states of every later unit were derived from the old prefix and can
838	        # no longer be adopted: cross-boundary links must be re-derived too.
839	        desynced = False
840	        # Per-tenant tripwire: earliest global index at which a tenant has a
841	        # record in a content-hash-failed window. Acts on tenants whose own
842	        # chain nevertheless re-derives (a recomputed-digest forgery).
843	        suspect: dict[str, int] = {}
844	
845	        for unit in units:
846	            name = unit["name"]
847	            path = unit["path"]
848	            try:
849	                stat = os.stat(path)
850	            except FileNotFoundError:
851	                if name == _FILE_UNIT:
852	                    # The legacy file does not exist before the first append.
853	                    continue
854	                raise
855	            entry = cached.get(name)
856	            entry_fold = entry.get("fold") if entry is not None else None
857	
858	            if (
859	                entry is not None
860	                and entry_fold is not None
861	                and not desynced
862	                and self._entry_fresh(entry, stat, unit)
863	            ):
864	                self._adopt_states(states, entry)
865	                total_records = entry["records"]
866	                entries[name] = _cache_entry(
867	                    total_records, stat, entry["parts"], states, entry_fold
868	                )
869	                continue
870	
871	            growth = (
872	                entry is not None
873	                and entry_fold is not None
874	                and not desynced
875	                and not unit["sealed"]
876	                and stat.st_size > entry["size"]
877	                and entry.get("parts", []) == unit["parts"]
878	            )
879	            if growth:
880	                # Appended-only growth on the active unit. Before the cache's
881	                # cumulative states are continued, the bytes the cache was
882	                # built on authenticate themselves byte for byte: a fold over
883	                # every complete line up to the cached size must equal the
884	                # fold stored in the (tag-authenticated) cache. A rewritten
885	                # prefix -- stale digests, recomputed digests, edited bytes
886	                # behind preserved manifest windows, a shifted boundary --
887	                # changes that fold, so the continuation is refused and the
888	                # walk falls through to a complete re-derivation, whose
889	                # verdict equals a full verification and whose first bad
890	                # index is the real position rather than the first new line.
891	                #
892	                # The writer warming the cache for the line it just appended
893	                # still holds the exclusive lock and the prefix is unchanged
894	                # by construction, so it extends the fold over the new lines
895	                # only.
896	                if trust_growth:
897	                    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
898	                        handle.seek(entry["size"])
899	                        tail_raw = handle.read()
900	                    tail_lines = _split_whole_lines(tail_raw)
901	                    if tail_lines is not None:
902	                        candidate = {
903	                            tenant: list(state) for tenant, state in states.items()
904	                        }
905	                        self._adopt_states(candidate, entry)
906	                        before_bad = {
907	                            tenant: state[2] for tenant, state in candidate.items()
908	                        }
909	                        tail_records = st.decode_records(b"".join(tail_lines))
910	                        self._apply_records(tail_records, candidate)
911	                        tail_broken = any(
912	                            state[2] != before_bad.get(tenant, -1)
913	                            for tenant, state in candidate.items()
914	                        )
915	                        new_fold = _extend_fold(entry_fold, tail_lines)
916	                    else:
917	                        candidate = None
918	                        tail_broken = True
919	                        new_fold = entry_fold
920	                    if candidate is not None and not tail_broken:
921	                        states.clear()
922	                        states.update(candidate)
923	                        total_records = entry["records"] + len(tail_records)
924	                        # Appended-only growth leaves the preserved prefix
925	                        # windows untouched, so carry their material in the
926	                        # cache.
927	                        entries[name] = _cache_entry(
928	                            total_records, stat, entry.get("parts", []), states, new_fold
929	                        )
930	                        continue
931	                else:
932	                    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
933	                        raw = handle.read()
934	                    prefix_raw = raw[: entry["size"]]
935	                    tail_raw = raw[entry["size"] :]
936	                    prefix_lines = _split_whole_lines(prefix_raw)
937	                    tail_lines = _split_whole_lines(tail_raw)
938	                    prefix_ok = (
939	                        prefix_lines is not None
940	                        and _fold_lines(prefix_lines) == entry_fold
941	                    )
942	                    if prefix_ok and tail_lines is not None:
943	                        candidate = {
944	                            tenant: list(state)
945	                            for tenant, state in states.items()
946	                        }
947	                        self._adopt_states(candidate, entry)
948	                        before_bad = {
949	                            tenant: state[2] for tenant, state in candidate.items()
950	                        }
951	                        tail_records = st.decode_records(b"".join(tail_lines))
952	                        self._apply_records(tail_records, candidate)
953	                        tail_broken = any(
954	                            state[2] != before_bad.get(tenant, -1)
955	                            for tenant, state in candidate.items()
956	                        )
957	                        if not tail_broken:
958	                            states.clear()
959	                            states.update(candidate)
960	                            total_records = entry["records"] + len(tail_records)
961	                            new_fold = _extend_fold(entry_fold, tail_lines)
962	                            entries[name] = _cache_entry(
963	                                total_records,
964	                                stat,
965	                                entry.get("parts", []),
966	                                states,
967	                                new_fold,
968	                            )
969	                            continue
970	                    # Prefix authentication failed or the boundary moved:
971	                    # re-derive this unit completely below.
972	
973	            # Cold unit, shrink, same-size rewrite, any change to a sealed
974	            # unit, a unit following one that desynced, or a growth whose
975	            # cached prefix failed authentication: full parse; sealed windows
976	            # are re-authenticated and every link is re-derived.
977	            desynced = True
978	            walked, parts, failed_tenants, fold = self._walk_bytes(unit, states)
979	            for tenant, index in failed_tenants.items():
980	                suspect.setdefault(tenant, index)
981	            if entry is not None:
982	                # The surviving cache anchors what this unit's per-tenant
983	                # heads and counts must be. Legitimate writes take the
984	                # growth branch above (or drop the cache via recover), so a
985	                # stat change landing here whose re-derived heads differ is
986	                # a rewritten history even when its digests recompute.
987	                for tenant, anchored in entry["tenants"].items():
988	                    current = states.get(tenant)
989	                    if current is None:
990	                        suspect.setdefault(tenant, 0)
991	                    elif (
992	                        current[0] != anchored[0] or current[1] != anchored[1]
993	                    ) and current[2] == -1:
994	                        suspect.setdefault(tenant, 0)
995	                if stat.st_size < entry["size"]:
996	                    # Records were deleted while the cache survived: flag the
997	                    # first missing global index for each affected tenant.
998	                    for tenant, anchored in entry["tenants"].items():
999	                        current = states.get(tenant)
1000	                        remaining = current[0] if current is not None else 0
1001	                        if remaining < anchored[0]:
1002	                            suspect.setdefault(tenant, remaining)
1003	            total_records += walked
1004	            entries[name] = _cache_entry(total_records, stat, parts, states, fold)
1005	
1006	        # A chain break attributes first_bad precisely and is used as-is.
1007	        # Separately, every tenant with a record in a content-hash-failed
1008	        # window whose own chain still re-derives is flagged: its bytes were
1009	        # rewritten with recomputed digests and must not pass. This is
1010	        # evaluated per tenant, so a real break in another tenant's chain
1011	        # never suppresses it.
1012	        for tenant, index in suspect.items():
1013	            state = states.get(tenant)
1014	            if state is not None and state[2] == -1:
1015	                state[2] = index
1016	
1017	        # Never warm the cache from a walk that saw corruption: otherwise a
1018	        # manifest whose window anchors were rewritten would, on a second
1019	        # verify, match its own (bad) cached parts and take the constant hot
1020	        # path straight to a false pass. A corrupt tree is re-derived from
1021	        # bytes on every verify until it is genuinely repaired.
1022	        any_bad = any(state[2] != -1 for state in states.values())
1023	        if persist and not suspect and not any_bad:
1024	            st.save_cache(layout, entries)
1025	        return (
1026	            {tenant: (state[0], state[1], state[2]) for tenant, state in states.items()},
1027	            entries,
1028	        )

1030	    @staticmethod
1031	    def _adopt_states(states: dict[str, list], entry: dict) -> None:
1032	        for tenant, state in entry["tenants"].items():
1033	            count, digest, bad = state
1034	            current = states.get(tenant)
1035	            if current is None:
1036	                states[tenant] = [count, digest, bad]
1037	            else:
1038	                # Never let a cached -1 erase an earlier first_bad.
1039	                prior_bad = current[2]
1040	                if prior_bad != -1 and (bad == -1 or prior_bad < bad):
1041	                    bad = prior_bad
1042	                states[tenant] = [count, digest, bad]

1044	    @staticmethod
1045	    def _stat_fresh(entry: dict, stat: os.stat_result, *, exact: bool = True) -> bool:
1046	        # size + mtime identify an unchanged append-only file; ctime (which
1047	        # utimes cannot restore) exposes a same-size content rewrite. The
1048	        # growth branch only needs size-growth + unchanged ctime.
1049	        if entry["ctime_ns"] != stat.st_ctime_ns:
1050	            return False
1051	        if not exact:
1052	            return entry["size"] <= stat.st_size
1053	        return (
1054	            entry["size"] == stat.st_size
1055	            and entry["mtime_ns"] == stat.st_mtime_ns
1056	        )

1058	    @staticmethod
1059	    def _entry_fresh(entry: dict, stat: os.stat_result, unit: dict) -> bool:
1060	        """Hot-path freshness with constant read amplification.
1061	
1062	        The size + mtime + ctime guard identifies an unchanged append-only
1063	        file (ctime exposes a same-size content rewrite and cannot be
1064	        restored). In addition, whenever the unit carries preserved byte
1065	        windows -- always for a sealed unit, and for an active unit after a
1066	        fold-to-one compaction -- the manifest's window material must match
1067	        what the cache authenticated, so an edited manifest window forces
1068	        the cold path and is reported as corruption, without a single sealed
1069	        byte being hashed on the ordinary path.
1070	        """
1071	        if not Chain._stat_fresh(entry, stat):
1072	            return False
1073	        cached_parts = entry.get("parts", [])
1074	        if unit["sealed"] or cached_parts or unit["parts"]:
1075	            return cached_parts == unit["parts"]
1076	        return True

1078	    def _walk_bytes(
1079	        self, unit: dict, states: dict[str, list]
1080	    ) -> tuple[int, list[dict], dict, str]:
1081	        """Parse and chain one unit's bytes.
1082	
1083	        Returns ``(record_count, cache_parts, failed_tenants, fold)`` where
1084	        ``failed_tenants`` maps each tenant with a record in a
1085	        content-hash-failed window to that record's global index, and
1086	        ``fold`` is the extendable byte fingerprint of the unit's complete
1087	        lines.
1088	
1089	        Content tampering normally breaks the victim's digest chain, which
1090	        attributes ``first_bad`` precisely and leaves tenants with no record
1091	        in the damaged window untouched. The window hash is an independent
1092	        tripwire: it only needs to act when the attacker also recomputed
1093	        digests (a clean-looking but rewritten log).
1094	        """
1095	        path = unit["path"]
1096	        windows = unit["parts"]
1097	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1098	            raw = handle.read()
1099	
1100	        failed: set[int] = set()
1101	        window_ends: list[int] = []
1102	        if windows:
1103	            if unit["sealed"] and len(raw) != sum(
1104	                window["size"] for window in windows
1105	            ):
1106	                failed.update(range(len(windows)))
1107	            elif not st.verify_prefix_windows(path, windows):
1108	                failed.update(range(len(windows)))
1109	            running = 0
1110	            for window in windows:
1111	                running += window["size"]
1112	                window_ends.append(running)
1113	
1114	        try:
1115	            text = raw.decode(_ENCODING)
1116	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
1117	            raise ValueError("malformed audit record") from exc
1118	        lines = rec.split_records(text)
1119	
1120	        first_index: dict[str, int] = {}
1121	        win_index = 0
1122	        pos = 0
1123	        for line in lines:
1124	            length = len((line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING))
1125	            start, end = pos, pos + length
1126	            pos = end
1127	            while win_index < len(window_ends) and start >= window_ends[win_index]:
1128	                win_index += 1
1129	            past_end = win_index >= len(window_ends)
1130	            crosses = not past_end and end > window_ends[win_index]
1131	            window_failed = not past_end and win_index in failed
1132	
1133	            record = rec.parse_line(line)
1134	            tenant = record["tenant"]
1135	            count, head, bad = states.get(tenant, [0, "", -1])
1136	            if window_failed:
1137	                first_index.setdefault(tenant, count)
1138	            if crosses:
1139	                # Windows only ever concatenate whole lines, so a record may
1140	                # never straddle a window boundary.
1141	                if bad == -1:
1142	                    bad = count
1143	            if unit["sealed"] and past_end and bad == -1:
1144	                # Bytes appended past a sealed segment's frozen material.
1145	                bad = count
1146	            recomputed = rec.digest(record["prev"], record["payload"])
1147	            if record["prev"] != head or record["digest"] != recomputed:
1148	                if bad == -1:
1149	                    bad = count
1150	            states[tenant] = [count + 1, record["digest"], bad]
1151	
1152	        # Sealed units carry their full window material; an active unit
1153	        # carries preserved *prefix* windows after a fold-to-one compaction.
1154	        # Both are retained in the cache so the hot-path freshness guard
1155	        # compares the manifest's window material for either kind.
1156	        parts = [dict(part) for part in windows]
1157	        # split_records guaranteed raw ends in a terminator, so this folds
1158	        # every complete line exactly as the continuation branch will.
1159	        fold = _fold_of_bytes(raw)
1160	        return len(lines), parts, first_index, fold
